title: Two-VM Callback Troubleshooting Lab
description: Trace and repair a harmless synthetic HTTP heartbeat between an isolated Ubuntu Sender and Listener. Practice Linux service, address, port, routing, name-resolution and firewall troubleshooting.

drills.title: Sender service is stopped
drills.brief: The Listener is healthy, but no synthetic heartbeat arrives. Check the Sender service, process and logs.
drills.goal: Restore the Sender service and verify a new heartbeat reaches the Listener.

drills.title: Sender targets the wrong address
drills.brief: The Sender service is active, but its configured destination is another address on the isolated practice subnet.
drills.goal: Correct the Listener address and verify a new heartbeat arrives.

drills.title: Listener port mismatch
drills.brief: The Listener listens on TCP 8080 while the Sender is configured to use a different port.
drills.goal: Correct the Sender port and restore heartbeat delivery.

drills.title: Listener service is stopped
drills.brief: The Sender retries its HTTP request, but the Listener process is not running.
drills.goal: Restore the Listener service and verify a new request is recorded.

drills.title: Listener is bound to loopback
drills.brief: The Listener service is active on port 8080 but accepts connections only from its own loopback interface.
drills.goal: Bind the service to the practice interface and confirm the Sender can reach it.

drills.title: Sender firewall blocks outbound traffic
drills.brief: The Sender service and destination are correct, but a host OUTPUT rule drops TCP 8080 packets to the Listener.
drills.goal: Remove only the blocking egress rule and restore the heartbeat.

drills.title: Listener firewall blocks inbound traffic
drills.brief: The Sender transmits to the right address and port, but a Listener INPUT rule drops packets from its paired Sender.
drills.goal: Remove only the blocking ingress rule and verify a new heartbeat.

drills.title: Invalid host route diverts traffic
drills.brief: The connected subnet route is correct, but a more-specific route sends the Listener traffic toward an unavailable next hop.
drills.goal: Remove the invalid route and restore direct reachability on the isolated subnet.
drills.tools: ip route, ip route get, ip neigh

drills.title: Listener hostname resolves to the wrong address
drills.brief: The Sender uses listener.training.local, but its local hosts entry maps the name to an unused practice address.
drills.goal: Correct local name resolution and verify the service recovers.

drills.title: Capstone: diagnose two simultaneous faults
drills.brief: The Listener receives no heartbeat. The Sender uses the wrong TCP port and an invalid more-specific route. Fix both without weakening the isolated network policy.
drills.goal: Restore the route and TCP port, then verify a new source-validated heartbeat reaches the Listener.
drills.tools: ip route get, ip route, ss, curl, journalctl
